judged_text: The create action changed its accepted envelope from nested params[:group][:name]/[:usernames]/[:visible] to flat params[:name]/[:visible], silently discarding the usernames field. Existing API consumers posting group[name]=x&group[usernames]=a,b get a 200 with a created group that has none of the requested members — the old create seeded membership atomically with creation and this behavior is gone with no error or version bump, so callers believe members were added.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows Admin::GroupsController#create was changed to read flat params (params[:name], params[:visible]) and no longer reads params[:group] nor assigns any usernames/membership (old code: group.usernames = params[:group][:usernames]). Membership is now handled via separate add_members/remove_member endpoints. This is a backwards-incompatible API/contract change for callers posting group[name]/group[usernames], but the finding’s claim that such callers would still get a 200 with an empty-members group isn’t directly verifiable (with only nested params, params[:name] would be nil and group save may fail).
